paragraphs.text: Dear sisters and elders, I hope you found joy in your service today. Each day brings us new opportunities and new challenges and usually they are the same thing.

As I've held zone interviews today, I've been asking some of the missionaries what were they learning from the challenge of being confined to the apartment but still being under the obligation to share the gospel because it almost seems like it's a contradiction, right? I can't leave the apartment but I've still got to share the gospel. I've heard many great answers to my question which really have inspired me and gave me confidence that the Quezon City North missionaries are thinking the right way about challenges actually being opportunities to learn.

One missionary asked me what I thought was the best learning from this challenge. I said that I believe that the great learning opportunity that each of us should learn from the COVID-19 quarantine is that we are able to adapt to a completely new environment and still succeed. I told this missionary that the world he was going to live most of his life in was very different from the world that I've lived most of my life in.

My young friends, your world is going to move faster and faster with changes in technology, medicine, everything. Quite frankly, every area of your life is just going to be really changing quickly and it's going to be changing for the better. But change is change.

Now during my father's days there wasn't very much change. The rule was you find the best job you knew how to find and you stay there your whole life and that would be your working career. There wouldn't be really much change. My father did his working years between 1945 and 1985 and there was very little change. The kind of telephone he used in '45 was the same kind of telephone he used in 1985. The kind of car he was driving in '45 wasn't very much different from the car that he was going to be driving in 1985. There was some change during those years but not a lot.

During my working years of 1980 to 2020 there's been a lot more change. We've got cell phones and the first cell phone, I remember I bought one of the first cell phones and it was like this big old brick and it was about the size of a narrow laptop. And now we got these little tiny smart phones that are more powerful than the gigantic computers that they used to use back about 40 years ago. So there was a lot more change in my 40 years than there was in my father's 40 years of working career. I had four different careers, not just one. He had one, I had four.
It's interesting that as I think about how this played out is my ability to succeed was largely driven by my ability to adapt to a new environment.

Now, if we think about this during my working years there was a lot more change but during your working years there's going to be an order of magnitude, perhaps several orders of magnitude more change than there was in my time. It's going to be stunning what's going to happen in the next 40 years. It's going to be wonderful in so many powerful ways but you're not going to be able to take advantage of it if you don't know how to adapt to change successfully, to be resilient and flexible. The people in your generation who know how to learn and learn fast are going to be the people who really enjoy and prosper in the next 40 years. So think about how this quarantine has given you the opportunity to exercise your creative muscles and become stronger in your resilience and adaptability.

When big change happens suddenly to most people they tend to freeze. They don't know what to do. Should they go right or left? Should they go forward or backward? Most do nothing because they can't decide what to do. It's like they're set on one way and when that way closes they just can't think about anything except what they used to do.

There's an old saying that goes like this, "when one door closes another one opens." It's a true saying but most people don't understand its truth because when their normal door closes they just stand there looking at the closed door. Maybe feeling sorry for themselves, maybe complaining, maybe criticizing but to see the open door you must say to yourself I know there's another door that's open somewhere and then you got to start looking around to find it. The people who do that get moving and they find the open doors and they make great progress while the other person's still staring at the closed door.

You are learning this very principle right now and you will be so much better prepared for what lies ahead in your life because you know this now. However, knowing is not enough. You must act to really benefit.

Understanding and accepting the mindset of resilience and adaptability is the most important first step but the second step is almost well maybe just as important. You must learn the skills as well. Learning the skills take action. You have to get right into your growth zone which means you've got to get right out of your comfort zone.

In the growth zone you practice those new skills. Will you be great at first? Of course not. You'll probably be not very good at all. People may even make fun of you. You may make fun of yourself. Don't worry about it because action makes you better and the better you get the more comfortable you will be. Pretty soon what was the growth zone has become the comfort zone and now you've got this big comfort zone that you can live in but you're not content there anymore because you like the idea of growth and so you step again outside of the comfort zone and you're looking for new growth and you're okay with that. You're not afraid of being in the growth zone anymore because you've experienced it enough times to know that it's just a matter of time until the growth zone becomes your new comfort zone.

This is Heavenly Father's plan. We talk about it all the time. Eternal progression. Lots of missionaries talk about eternal progression, even teach it, but they sometimes have a hard time living it and to live it you must really really understand that being uncomfortable is the first step towards growing into an eternal mindset of progression. You have to live eternal progression if you want to truly follow the Savior. So keep learning, keep growing, keep looking for the open doors that will allow you to fulfill your purpose even under the confinement we are now required to experience.

You're not the only people to take advantage of hardship to grow and to serve. Shakespeare wrote his famous plays King Lear and Macbeth and several others while he was in a quarantine for the bubonic plague that struck London during his life. Sir Isaac Newton discovered and explained the principle of gravity and other mathematical principles while he was quarantined.

Joseph Smith wrote the inspired letters which are now Doctrine and Covenants section 121 and 122 while he was in Liberty Jail. I'm sure there are many other examples but I think you get the point. Use this time to grow and learn. Be resilient and adaptable. Use your precious time and technology wisely and you will always be grateful you did.

Now early this morning I received a letter through email from the First Presidency informing Mission Presidents of some more adjustments to missionary service. I will post that letter in the adjustments to messenger later on tonight so be looking for that.

And just a few minutes ago I received an email from the Area Presidency informing the leaders of the church in the Philippines that the church has arranged for general conference to be broadcast on a couple of national TV stations right here in the Philippines. I will also post this letter in the details to messenger so you can know and be able to you know inform members and investigators how they can watch conference in their own homes.

Sisters and elders this is a great time of life. I hope you're enjoying it. I hope you enjoy this evening. And always remember that gratitude is the mother of all virtues. If you will grow your gratitude you will find all the other virtues coming into your life more easily. I'm grateful for you and for a loving Heavenly Father whose power is over us all. Good night and God bless you.
